name: manual_5bb056
claim: A stray package-lock.json alongside a canonical pnpm-lock.yaml isn't just dead weight -- it actively misleads Dependabot into 'fixing' a file nothing reads, masking the real unpatched vulnerability

decisions.notes: orama-system/web/package-lock.json was correctly deleted 2026-06-12 during the npm-to-pnpm migration (commit 5f37488b, message: 'Drop package-lock.json in favor of pnpm-lock.yaml'), then accidentally resurrected 2026-07-13 by an unrelated commit whose message admits 'Also committing web/package-lock.json (untracked from a fresh npm install)' -- someone ran plain npm install in web/ on a machine without pnpm set up, and it rode along with an unrelated Windows-docs commit. Dependabot's npm_and_yarn bot then found this resurrected file and 'fixed' the js-yaml CVE in it (2026-08-08, commit bba9f06c) -- but the REAL lockfile, pnpm-lock.yaml, has js-yaml pinned via pnpm-workspace.yaml's overrides: block, which Dependabot's automated PR generator doesn't understand or edit. Net effect: a Dependabot PR that LOOKED like it fixed the CVE, merged clean, and the alert stayed open for 2 more weeks because the real file was untouched. General lesson: when a repo has multiple lockfiles for one package manager transition, an accidentally-resurrected dead one isn't harmless clutter -- delete it immediately on sight, don't just leave it; it will eventually eat a real security fix.
